headline: No SAC-vs-RLPD claim is supportable: SAC's two training seeds disagree more than SAC differs from RLPD.

SAC_seed1.note: n=25 only; no saved 414k checkpoint (predates per-step retention)

evidence_414k_frozen_suite.reading: RLPD sits BETWEEN the two SAC seeds. SAC s1 and SAC s2 have non-overlapping carry intervals despite being the SAME algorithm.

correction: an earlier report of mine said RLPD underperformed SAC on every primary metric. That compared RLPD against SAC seed 1 alone. With SAC seed 2 measured at n=50, SAC s2 carries 0.00 at the same checkpoint -- worse than RLPD's 0.12. The direction of the comparison depends entirely on which SAC seed is picked, which is precisely why the claim is unsupportable.

posthoc_reproduces_training.note: RLPD reproduces exactly; SAC s2 differs by one condition (0.04 = 1/25), within GPU nondeterminism for a contact-rich task

what_IS_supported: both algorithms take grasp from the SFT baseline of 0.02 to ~1.00; that holds across every seed and checkpoint measured
required_next: the three missing training arms (RLPD s2, SAC s3, RLPD s3). With 3 seeds per method the seed distribution can be separated from the algorithm difference; with 2 vs 1 it cannot.
